semantic_runtime_health.definition: classified_coverage = (MATCHED + NONE) / eligible_claim_count. The >=95% figure is an INTERNAL_ENGINEERING_RUNTIME_BENCHMARK (Step 5A) -- never a John release gate, regression acceptance, or semantic-accuracy claim.
semantic_runtime_health.honest_finding: 3 of 6 tickers (NVDA 45.99%, MSFT 3.92%, TSM 0.00%) FAILED the internal 95% runtime-health benchmark due to severe DeepSeek 'provider_error' storms (435, 659, and 793 provider_error events respectively) during Week2 semantic classification -- NOT a code or semantic-prompt defect (production semantic code was frozen throughout this task; see semantic_changes_made). 3 of 6 tickers (QQQ 98.34%, SNDK 98.44%, AMD 97.39%) met the benchmark cleanly. A real-world wall-clock gap of ~14 hours was observed between the QQQ and MSFT runs in this same process (started_at/ended_at vs. the much shorter monotonic elapsed_seconds), consistent with the host machine suspending/resuming during MSFT's execution window -- a plausible (not certain) contributing factor to that specific ticker's provider-error storm, noted honestly rather than asserted as proven. This is reported, not repaired, per task section 28: no tuning, no retry for semantic-quality reasons, no silent re-run.

john_historical_alpha_callouts.step5b_comparison: Step 5B (healthy, isolated semantic validation) found 12/12 DETECTED. This fresh live E2E run found 7/12 DETECTED -- the 5 misses are on MSFT (A101/A102/A304) and TSM (A103/A304), the exact two tickers that failed semantic runtime health above (3.92% and 0.00% coverage). All 5 are classified NOT_DETECTED_SOURCE_PRESENT/PROVIDER_FAILURE, not a semantic recall regression -- the Step 5B 12/12 finding does not reproduce here because this specific run's runtime health degraded on those two tickers, not because Alpha Mapper semantics changed (they did not).
